Downtown is the historic core of Chilliwack Proper, centred on Five Corners, where Yale Road and Young Road intersect with Wellington Avenue.
The downtown core centres on Main Street, Yale Road East and Young Road, with First Avenue and Princess Avenue framing the District 1881 blocks.

Municipally this ground is planned as Schedule B3, the Downtown Neighbourhood Plan, inside the Chilliwack 2050 Official Community Plan (OCP); it is a Chilliwack and District Real Estate Board (CADREB) market, not a Fraser Valley board market.

The downtown form is set by plan, not by a housing count: the Downtown Neighbourhood Plan directs land use, housing, commercial and economic vitality, public open space and the form and character of development for the core.
District 1881 itself mixes retail, commercial, residential and mixed-use buildings in one redevelopment, including the Woolworth Flats homes at 46128 Yale Road named on the developer's own site.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Downtown: rules that affect buyers

items.t: The Chilliwack Downtown Design Guidelines under D-6 direct new development to use the form, proportion, pattern and detailing of the core's existing fabric, and encourage restoration of buildings of heritage value using historically accurate materials.

The City's December 2025 guide confirms a development permit is required for new construction, additions, signs and significant site alterations in Development Permit Areas 6 to 10, including DPA 6 Downtown.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Downtown: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Chilliwack Library, 45860 First Avenue, is the Fraser Valley Regional Library branch inside the core.
Chilliwack General Hospital, 45600 Menholm Road, is immediately north of the core and provides emergency care.

The Chilliwack Mural Festival's street party runs in District 1881 and on Mill Street, with District 1881's Thunderbird Stage and a Breezeway performance space off Yale Road — a recurring road-activity weekend in the core.
City Hall, the permit counter for D-6 applications, is at 8550 Young Road, at the core's south edge.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Downtown: development and new projects

items.t: District 1881, Five Corners site bounded by Young Road, Yale Road, Princess Avenue and Empress Lane, developer Algra Bros. Developments Ltd.: a multi-year, multi-phase mix of retail, commercial, residential and mixed-use buildings on the 3.75-acre City/CEPCO assembly. STATUS: built phases operating, project described by CEPCO as the benchmark redevelopment for subsequent downtown development, read 2026-11-03.
Downtown Neighbourhood Plan (Schedule B3): adopted June 2010, updated 2025 as part of Official Community Plan Bylaw 2025, No. 5500. STATUS: current plan, read 2026-11-03.

The downtown-specific cost is process: a D-6 development permit application, with design-guideline compliance, is part of the budget for new construction, additions, signs and significant site alterations in the core.
Downtown Chilliwack is the main British Columbia Transit (BC Transit) exchange and terminus for local routes 51 to 59, 71 and 72.
Route 66 Fraser Valley Express runs from Downtown Chilliwack to Lougheed Town Centre Station, with Chilliwack stops including Vedder Road at Luckakuck Way and the Lickman Park & Ride.
BC Transit's December 18, 2025 service notice, effective January 4, 2026, added Sunday-evening service for Route 57 Broadway, Route 53 Fairfield and Route 51.

blocks.text: Chilliwack Downtown: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check which Schedule D permit areas touch the parcel, not just D-6: the OCP lists D-1 Drinking Water Supply through D-10 Industrial, and areas beyond D-6 apply per parcel.
Heritage value is a permit factor downtown: the D-6 guidelines encourage restoration of buildings of heritage value and direct historically accurate exterior materials for that work.

Chilliwack Downtown home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

27 condos sold in Chilliwack Downtown with a median price of $288,000 (the middle half sold between $226,250 and $375,750), taking a median of 33 days to sell at 96.9% of the last list price; 4% sold above list. They had a median $322 per square foot, a median year built of 1993 and a median strata fee of $415 a month. 3 houses sold in Chilliwack Downtown, too few (5 needed) to give a typical price.

faq.a: The Downtown Neighbourhood Plan, Schedule B3 of the Chilliwack 2050 OCP. Adopted in June 2010 and updated in 2025, it sets the vision for the Downtown Plan Area over 30 years, covering land use, housing, commercial vitality, open space, transportation and the form and character of both public and private development. Read the parcel's designation in B3 before valuing any infill potential.
faq.q: Which plan actually governs a downtown purchase?

faq.a: District 1881 is the redevelopment of the 3.75-acre downtown site bounded by Young Road, Yale Road, Princess Avenue and Empress Lane. The City of Chilliwack and the Chilliwack Economic Partners Corporation (CEPCO) assembled the properties, and Council awarded the redevelopment contract to Algra Bros. Developments Ltd. The project combines retail, commercial, residential and mixed-use buildings across multiple phases.
faq.q: What is District 1881, and who built it?

New work is expected to fit the core's form, proportion and detailing, and buildings of heritage value are encouraged to be restored with historically accurate materials, so exterior plans need a permit check first.
